'''Alanyaspor Kulübü''', known as '''Corendon Alanyaspor''' for sponsorship reasons, is a Turkish professional football club based in the city of [[Alanya]] in [[Antalya Province]]. The team have competed in the [[Süper Lig]] since their first-ever promotion to the top flight in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |date=31 May 2016 |title=Alanyaspor promoted to Turkey's top league |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/alanyaspor-promoted-to-turkeys-top-league/585919 |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Anadolu Agency}}</ref> Home matches are played at the [[Alanya Oba Stadium]], a compact, all-seater ground with a capacity of 9,789.<ref>{{cite web |date=27 May 2019 |title=Alanyaspor 9.789 kapasiteli Oba Stadı'na veda ediyor |url=https://ajansspor.com/haber/alanyaspor-9789-kapasiteli-oba-stadina-veda-ediyor-326173 |access-date=15 August 2025 |website=Ajansspor |language=tr}}</ref>

The club's traditional colours are orange and green, adopted in 1982 following a statute change.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 July 2020 |title=Ziraat Türkiye Kupası Finali – Medya Dosyası |url=https://www.tff.org/Resources/TFF/Documents/Turkiye-Kupasi/2020/2020-Final-Media-Kit.pdf |access-date=15 August 2025 |publisher=Turkish Football Federation |language=tr}}</ref> In June 2022 the club confirmed a naming-rights agreement with [[Corendon Airlines|Corendon]], after which the professional football team have competed as Corendon Alanyaspor.<ref>{{cite news |date=21 June 2022 |title=Alanyaspor'un ismi Corendon Alanyaspor oluyor |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/alanyasporun-ismi-corendon-alanyaspor-oluyor-42103617 |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Hürriyet |language=tr}}</ref>

Founded in 1948, Alanyaspor rose through the national pyramid and established themselves in the top tier in the late 2010s. The club's best league finish to date is fifth place in the [[2019–20 Süper Lig]], a season in which they also reached the [[Turkish Cup]] final; [[Trabzonspor]] won the decider 2–0 in [[Istanbul]].<ref>{{cite news |date=27 July 2020 |title=Alanyaspor en iyi Süper Lig derecesiyle Avrupa kapısını araladı |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/futbol/alanyaspor-en-iyi-super-lig-derecesiyle-avrupa-kapisini-araladi/1923661 |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Anadolu Ajansı |language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=30 July 2020 |title=Trabzonspor win Ziraat Turkish Cup |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/trabzonspor-win-ziraat-turkish-cup-156463 |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Hürriyet Daily News}}</ref>

The same campaign qualified Alanyaspor for Europe for the first time; they entered the [[UEFA Europa League]] in 2020–21 and were eliminated 1–0 away to [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] in a single-leg third qualifying round tie played behind closed doors during the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite web |date=24 September 2020 |title=Rosenborg 1–0 Alanyaspor |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2030307--rosenborg-vs-alanyaspor/ |access-date=15 August 2025 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>"}}
